title: Indeed’s 2026 Organic Visibility Change: What It Means for Frontline Hiring
summary: Indeed's single-source feed change went live March 31, 2026. What changed, who it affects, and how frontline teams keep applicant flow steady.
body_markdown:
Indeed’s organic visibility change became effective March 31, 2026, and frontline employers are now hiring under it. Jobs sent to Indeed through single-source XML feeds no longer appear for free when those jobs could be delivered through an integrated


[applicant tracking system (ATS)](https://www.fountain.com/hire) .


Routing postings through an ATS with a


[direct Indeed integration](https://www.fountain.com/posts/save-time-with-fountains-new-direct-indeed-integration) is the primary move that keeps them eligible for free organic placement for


[frontline hiring](https://www.fountain.com/frontline-hiring) , where volume and speed are non-negotiable.


For


[QSR operators](https://www.fountain.com/2025-qsr-workforce-snapshot-report) , retailers, and logistics operators, reduced organic visibility can contribute to lower applicant flow at specific stores, and some employers may need to budget for sponsorship. Reduced applicant flow can leave shifts open and force managers to cover them.


## **What is Indeed’s organic visibility change?**


Indeed’s organic visibility change is a policy under which jobs delivered to Indeed through single-source XML feeds have not appeared for free since March 31, 2026, when those jobs could instead be sent through an ATS that Indeed has integrated with. An ATS with a direct Indeed integration keeps those jobs eligible.


Indeed’s single-source feed policy puts it this way: “Starting March 31, 2026, jobs sent through single-source XML feeds will no longer appear for free if they can be sent through an Applicant Tracking System (ATS).” A single-source feed, in Indeed’s


[single-source feed definition](https://www.indeed.com/help/employers/articles/what-is-aggregation?hl=en&co=US) , “is a job feed that includes jobs from only one employer,” and is often built by the company itself or by an agency on its behalf.


Indeed also requires that route: “If your ATS is integrated with Indeed, you must use that integration to post jobs,” per its


[single-source feed policy](https://www.indeed.com/help/employers/articles/single-source-feed-policy-effective-march-31-2026?hl=en&co=US) . Indeed said in June that


[free organic visibility](https://www.ere.net/articles/indeed-turns-up-the-heat-on-free-job-postings) “is not guaranteed nor will it be consistent over time, particularly in competitive roles or locations.”


For employers using an ATS with no Indeed integration, including some homegrown systems, Indeed says the change does not apply to them right now. Indeed still indexes public


[career sites](https://www.fountain.com/posts/why-you-need-to-invest-in-your-career-site) , and employers who don’t migrate can


[retain organic traffic](https://www.hrdive.com/news/visibility-ends-for-certain-free-single-source-xml-feeds-on-indeed/816209) through scraped career pages.


The policy page says it standardizes how employers send jobs and “helps improve job quality and make hiring easier for employers.” Staffing agencies, RPOs, and other recruitment-based companies already had to


[sponsor every job](https://www.indeed.com/legal) under Indeed’s Terms of Service.


The


[policy’s key dates](https://www.indeed.com/help/employers/articles/single-source-feed-policy-effective-march-31-2026?hl=en&co=US) add two more single-source cutoffs, June 30 and December 31, 2026, for agency-built feeds, worth checking against your own setup now.


## **Why the change matters for frontline hiring teams**


Reduced free impressions can lower applicant volume, and frontline demand doesn’t pause while volume recovers. Accommodation and food services ran a 5.5% openings rate in


[March 2026](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/job-openings-rate-2-3-percent-in-wholesale-trade-5-5-percent-in-accommodation-and-food-services.htm) , among the highest of the sectors listed, and retail’s rate climbed 1.5 points year over year to 4.6%.


Losing free reach on a site with more than


[350 million global visitors](https://au.indeed.com/hire/resources/howtohub/indeed-analytics-and-hiring-insights) each month can further reduce already-low applicant volume.

- **Applicant volume falls as free impressions disappear.** Screening funnels start further behind when the top of the pipeline shrinks.


- **Cost per hire climbs when roles need sponsorship to stay visible,** and spending can scale with location count.


- **Frontline time-to-fill stretches** as thinner applicant pools push interviews and Day 1 back for managers already working short, and a


[time-to-fill calculator](https://www.fountain.com/discover/total-time-to-fill-calculator-with-attrition) can show the cost of each open shift.


- **Location-level consistency wobbles** because Indeed says competitive locations are where free placement is least consistent, so placement varies store to store across dozens or hundreds of sites.


Open your sourcing data and flag every location where Indeed supplies more than half of applicants, then shift part of that budget to referrals, SMS, or another board so a single ranking change can’t empty the pipeline.


## **What to do now**


Use a directly integrated ATS to preserve free-visibility eligibility, then diversify and measure sourcing channels so eligibility matters less. Route jobs through Fountain’s ATS and confirm the connection in Indeed’s Integration Hub: single-source feeds lose free placement, while the integrated route keeps jobs eligible for organic visibility.


- **Direct ATS integration and a clean career site keep jobs eligible for free placement.** Jobs still leaving through a single-source XML feed belong in an ATS that Indeed lists as integrated, and the


[Integration Hub](https://www.indeed.com/hire/c/info/what-is-ats) inside your Indeed employer account confirms whether a given ATS qualifies. Google’s


[JobPosting structured data documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/job-posting) lists the required properties (job title, description, hiring organization, address, validThrough) and calls for one posting per page with location data, so candidates can find each opening through the career site when board visibility fluctuates.


- **Indeed-organic exposure by role and location shows where the risk concentrates.** A look back at source data from before March 31 shows which stores, warehouses, or restaurants drew most of their applicants from free Indeed listings, so sponsorship and alternate channels can go there first.


- **Selective sponsorship protects the sites that actually need it.** Indeed offers


[sponsored jobs](https://www.indeed.com/hire/cs/pricing) for openings that need more visibility, and spending compounds across roles and locations, so reserve it for sites with documented volume gaps rather than sponsoring every opening.


- **Channels beyond Indeed spread the risk across sources.**[Targeted sourcing campaigns](https://www.fountain.com/reach) ,


[referral campaigns](https://www.fountain.com/pool) , CRM reactivation, and other job boards each take a share of the load.


- **Source-and-location measurement catches units at risk before they go short.** Track conversion, not just raw applicant counts, since volume alone can hide differences in source quality, and review impressions and click-to-apply by location weekly to spot declines early.


- **Speed matters more on the applicants who do arrive.** Ghosting and slow follow-up are common candidate frustrations, so a same-day interview and a mobile offer letter recover applicants a competitor would otherwise take.


This quarter, route jobs through an integrated ATS and compare applicant volume and cost by location each week. Teams that delay may need to buy sponsorship after applicant volume has already fallen.

## **Frequently asked questions about Indeed’s organic visibility change**


### **What is Indeed’s organic visibility change?**


Indeed’s organic visibility change removes free placement from jobs sent through a single-employer feed when those jobs could instead be delivered through an Indeed-integrated ATS. Jobs pushed to Indeed through a feed containing


[one employer’s postings](https://www.indeed.com/help/employers/articles/what-is-aggregation?hl=en&co=US) lose free placement in search results if those postings could have been delivered through an ATS that Indeed has integrated with. Jobs from integrated ATSs remain eligible for free placement, though Indeed says that placement is


[neither guaranteed nor consistent](https://www.ere.net/articles/indeed-turns-up-the-heat-on-free-job-postings) in competitive markets.


### **When did it take effect?**


The policy became effective March 31, 2026.


### **Does it affect every employer that posts on Indeed?**


No. Indeed’s policy applies when jobs can be delivered through an ATS that supports Indeed Apply. Staffing agencies and RPOs were already required to


[sponsor every job](https://www.indeed.com/legal) before the change.


### **How do I keep my jobs visible on Indeed for free?**


Your jobs stay eligible when they reach Indeed through a directly integrated ATS, which you can confirm in the Integration Hub inside your Indeed account. A


[public career site](https://www.hrdive.com/news/visibility-ends-for-certain-free-single-source-xml-feeds-on-indeed/816209) with one posting per page and location-specific structured data gives Indeed a second source to index. Competitive roles and metros may require selective sponsorship because neither path guarantees organic placement.


### **Is Indeed still worth it for frontline hiring?**


Yes. With its large global audience, Indeed can remain an important volume channel for frontline hiring. Selective sponsorship may be needed for more consistent placement, which makes Indeed one measured channel among several rather than the source of most of your applicant flow.
